doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Bolden-era musicians and the Johnson brothers of Algiers
summary: Mary and Allen try to name Bolden's band members, Frankie Dusen and others. They recall Buddy and Yank Johnson of Algiers, schoolmates of Mary.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Same type of music and dance bands too. Dance bands and everything. I was going to ask Mrs. McBride a little bit more about the early bands when you were even a little girl, the first dances you'd go to or when you'd hear if you can remember Buddy Bolden's band at all.
I do remember, yes. That was the band then. Because the trombone... I can't think of the name.
Do you remember there were a couple of trombonists that worked with Buddy Bolden, they tell me I didn't know them. Frankie Doosan. From Frankie Doosan, yes.
Oh, I see why.
My dear, I was trying to think. He looked like a Mexican. Frankie Doosan.
I've seen his picture, yes.

Yes, yes. He was of a dark complex with straight hair. Frankie Doosan. He came from Algiers too, Professor. Why, I know the whole family. I'm trying to think of all of them. But I just can't think it's been so long in no years. Frankie Doosan.

A banjo player, but I don't think he was from Algiers, the Brock Mumford. Who? Mumford, Brock. Brock? And then there was the Lorenzo Stahl. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. But they were from over on the other side, uptown on the other side of the river.

Yeah, well I knew Lorenzo Stahl for a pretty period too there, but he played with us once too. I think he went up on this trip when you said about, oh, his brother coming through the cane. Uh-huh. I think Lorenzo Stahl was with him. He was with Oliver. Oh, he was?
Yes, sure. Lorenzo, yeah.
Are you bringing up names? Of course, you were still down there, living there.
He's not living, but people tell me about him.

Oh, they're down there, but my goodness. We'd have to go way back. Now, as much as I followed the band, why, if somebody died, we'd wait for the funeral, for the band to be played behind them. And I'd know everybody that played in the band, but I can't think of them now.
Well, do you remember the Johnson brothers over in Algiers, Yank and Buddy Johnson, the trombone?
That's who I was trying to say, who played trombone? Buddy Johnson, Little Shortfella. Do you remember them, Matt? Yeah, I remember Buddy Johnson.
Yank? Yeah, I know all those fellas, knew them then.
Yank was a drummer. Yeah. Yank played drums.
I thought he played trombone too later, I think. Yes, yes.
But I think they both... Yank was the long-haired one. Mm-hmm.
I never knew them myself. Well, we knew them. I remember them now.

I know Buddy, I know Buddy Johnson, Little Shortfella, he was. Then Yank, his brother was bad. Yank was the bad boy. When we went to school together, he had long heads. Mm-hmm. Yeah. Yeah. And he was the kind of thing. Well, I reclaimed.
